0.0.n: Sets the time for the introduction.

0.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic, highlighting when the introduction happens.

0.3.n: This adjective directly describes お友だち.

0.4.n: Literally means friend; お adds a warm, polite touch, common when speaking to children.

0.5.n: Marks お友だち as the person being introduced.

0.6.n: 紹介します is the polite form of 紹介する, used here to announce an introduction.

1.0.n: This is the opening part of 初めまして, a set greeting used when meeting someone for the first time.

1.1.n: Completes 初めまして; まして is a polite linking form, not a separate greeting here.

1.3.n: ぼく is a personal pronoun commonly used by boys and men.

1.4.n: Links ぼく to 名前 to express whose name it is.

1.5.n: ぼくの名前 means the speaker's own name.

1.6.n: Marks ぼくの名前 as the topic being identified.

1.7.n: This is a person's name, written in katakana as foreign names usually are.

1.8.n: Politely ends the statement identifying the speaker's name.

2.0.n: In an introduction, this expression asks for goodwill and a friendly relationship.

2.1.n: Softens the greeting and invites a warm response from the listener.

0.lit: Today, as for, a new friend, I will introduce.
0.tip: 紹介します politely announces the introduction; the speaker's I is understood rather than stated.

1.lit: Meeting for the first time! As for my name, it is Alec.
1.tip: Treat 初めまして as one fixed greeting, even though it is split into two tappable parts.

2.tip: よろしくね is a casual, friendly introduction greeting, not a phrase to translate word for word.
